# Temple Scroll Column 23 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Temple Scroll Column 23 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 23:1 — "peace offerings" vs. "fellowship offerings"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "peace offerings" | Traditional rendering of shelamim |
| LOGOS | "peace offerings" | Standard scholarly English |
| PNEUMA | "fellowship offerings" | Captures the communal meal aspect of the sacrifice |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET/LOGOS: "peace offerings." This is the universally recognized rendering; "fellowship offerings" is an NIV innovation that imports interpretive assumptions.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 23:1 — "offering of your hands" vs. "voluntary offerings" vs. "freewill gifts"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "offering of your hands" | Literal translation of terumat yadeikhem |
| LOGOS | "voluntary offerings" | Interprets the idiom as describing freewill contributions |
| PNEUMA | "freewill gifts" | Modern phrasing of the same concept |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS: "voluntary offerings." The Hebrew idiom "offering of your hands" refers to manual contributions; LOGOS captures the meaning clearly. EMET's literal rendering is obscure.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 23:5 — "strange incense" vs. "unauthorized incense"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "strange incense" | Literal rendering of qetoret zarah |
| LOGOS | "unauthorized incense" | Clarifies that "strange" means "not prescribed" |
| PNEUMA | "unauthorized incense" | Same as LOGOS |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS/PNEUMA: "unauthorized incense." "Strange" in modern English does not convey the Hebrew sense of zar (alien to the prescribed ritual).

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/PNEUMA.

---

## 23:7 — "between the evenings" vs. "at twilight" vs. "late afternoon"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "between the evenings" | Literal rendering of bein ha-arbayim |
| LOGOS | "at twilight" | Standard scholarly equivalent |
| PNEUMA | "in the late afternoon" | Modern time reference based on rabbinic interpretation |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS: "at twilight." Captures the temporal sense without EMET's obscure literalism or PNEUMA's overly specific time designation.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 23:12 — "most holy" vs. "supremely sacred"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "most holy" | Standard rendering of qodesh qodashim |
| LOGOS | "most holy" | Traditional |
| PNEUMA | "supremely sacred" | Fresh English phrasing |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET/LOGOS: "most holy." Consistent with project-wide rendering of qodesh qodashim.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 23:13 — "beginnings of your months" vs. "beginning of each month" vs. "start of each month"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "beginnings of your months" | Preserves Hebrew plural roshei chodsheikhem |
| LOGOS | "beginning of each month" | Natural English singular |
| PNEUMA | "start of each month" | Modern phrasing |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS: "at the beginning of each month." Clear English that preserves the recurring monthly sense without the awkward plural.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---
